record.paper_title: THE LYAPIN’S NOTEBOOK: A COLLECTION OF UNSOLVED PROBLEMS IN SEMIGROUP THEORY
record.original_question: Describe, for known predicates, the semigroup varieties that are locally residually finite, meaning that every finitely generated semigroup in the variety is residually finite with respect to the predicate under consideration.

evidence.quote:
Problem 2.2. (S. Kublanovsky) Describe locally residually finite varieties of semigroups for known
predicates.
In the global case, such description is obtained in [11], [12]. For the equality predicate in the local
case, the description is obtained in [32]. Locally residually finite varieties of rings were described
in [13].

           Let RSn denote the variety generated by all 0-simple semigroups satisfying the identity
x2 = xn+2 . Such varieties and their subvarieties are called Rees-Sushkevich varieties (see [14]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let a predicate $P$ on semigroups be a property of pairs (or tuples) of elements, such as the equality predicate $x = y$, the divisibility predicates $x \mid y$ (right, left, or two-sided), membership in a given (principal) ideal, membership in a maximal subgroup, conjugacy, or other commonly studied semigroup-theoretic relations.

A semigroup $S$ is said to be residually finite with respect to a predicate $P$ if, whenever $P$ fails on a tuple of elements of $S$, there exists a homomorphism $\varphi: S \to F$ onto a finite semigroup $F$ such that $P$ also fails on the image tuple in $F$. (For the equality predicate this recovers the classical notion of residual finiteness.)

A variety $\mathcal{V}$ of semigroups is called locally residually finite with respect to $P$ if every finitely generated semigroup in $\mathcal{V}$ is residually finite with respect to $P$.

The problem: For each of the standard semigroup predicates (equality, the various divisibility predicates, membership in principal ideals, membership in maximal subgroups, and other classically considered predicates), give an explicit description—preferably in terms of identities or other effectively verifiable conditions—of all semigroup varieties that are locally residually finite with respect to that predicate.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an unsolved problem attributed to S. Kublanovsky in a contemporary collection of open problems in semigroup theory. While the global (non-local) case has been described, and the local case for the equality predicate is known, the description for general predicates in the local case appears to remain open.
